chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Sufi narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Aqeel narrated from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, saying:

When Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) arrived in Nishapur and wanted to depart from it to al-Ma'mun, the people of hadith gathered around him and said to him: O son of Allah's Messenger, will you leave us and not narrate a hadith to us from which we may benefit?

He was sitting in al-'Amariya, so he raised his head and said: I heard my father Musa ibn Ja'far say: I heard my father Ja'far ibn Muhammad say: I heard my father Muhammad ibn Ali say: I heard my father Ali ibn al-Husayn say: I heard my father al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib say: I heard my father the Commander of the Believers Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) say: I heard Jibra'il (peace be upon him) say: I heard Allah, Exalted and Glorious, say:
"There is no god but Allah is My Shield. Hence, the one who enters My Shield is safe from My punishment."
He said: Then, when the caravan walked, he called to us: With its conditions, and I am one of its conditions.

key_terms.حِصْنِي: My Shield (referring to the declaration of monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Allah's Shield' in Shia theology and how does one enter it?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, highlights the esoteric significance of the Shahada as 'Allah's Shield' (Hissn Allah), a concept deeply rooted in Shia theology where the declaration of monotheism serves as a divine refuge from punishment. The chain of narration (isnad) traces back through the Imams to the Prophet and ultimately to God, underscoring the Ahl al-Bayt's role as the authoritative transmitters of this spiritual guarantee. The concluding remark by Imam al-Rida, 'I am one of its conditions,' links the theological concept to the Imamate, suggesting that true entry into this shield requires adherence to the Imams as the practical manifestation of divine guidance.
